item.title: [github_trending] vercel-labs/agent-desktop
item.description: agent-desktop is an Apache-2.0 npm package from Vercel Labs that lets AI agents read and drive desktop apps on macOS, Windows and Linux through the OS accessibility tree, skipping screenshots and pixel matching. It targets developers who want agents to operate conventional desktop software without maintaining a vision pipeline.

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: A Juejin post works through a question that interviewers now ask: given that candidates are assumed to use AI, why should a company still hire you when AI already writes most of the code? The author contrasts this with interviews from two years ago, which still tested hand-written Promises and React Fiber internals, and argues the evaluation criteria have shifted. Useful for developers preparing for technical interviews right now.

item.title: [v2ex] [推广] ChatGPT Plus/Pro 长期稳定 直充账户
item.description: A V2EX promotional post selling direct top-ups for ChatGPT Plus and Pro accounts, priced at 125 for Plus, 660 for the 5x tier and 1150 for 20x, with invoices offered. The poster says Pro quotas have doubled and that the 5x tier delivers roughly ten times Plus usage, claims 100-plus V2EX users served, and asks buyers to add a WeChat contact with a note. Third-party account top-ups carry ownership and ban risks, so buyers should judge for themselves.

item.title: [infoq] 构建面向 Agentic 推理的下一代 LLM 推理引擎
item.description: TokenSpeed, presented by independent contributor Shang Xuchun at AICon 2026 Shenzhen, is an inference engine built for agentic workloads: rather than maximizing batch throughput, it targets the highest per-GPU throughput that still keeps each user above 70 TPS. On that basis it reports 9% lower end-to-end latency than TensorRT-LLM at batch size 1. The talk also covers a decoupled architecture, auto-parallel compilation and KV Cache reuse — useful for anyone tuning inference for multi-turn coding

item.description: HackerTube is a project that builds a YouTube-style browsing experience out of videos that have been recommended on Hacker News. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

item.description: A developer is promoting browseraigames.com on V2EX, a site with separate sections for playing AI-made browser games and for building your own. The post says game creation is supported by Opus 5.5, which makes it worth a look for anyone wanting to prototype small browser games with low setup cost.

item.title: [infoq] 前迪士尼 AI 高管出任 CPO，Utopai Studios 技术布局再提速
item.description: Utopai Studios has hired Hans Ku, formerly VP of AI and engineering in Walt Disney's technology enablement office, as chief product officer, putting him in charge of product, engineering, research and business development to scale its PAI long-form narrative engine. At Disney he helped bridge OpenAI's research and product teams on Sora; at Tubi he shipped a GPT-4-powered content discovery feature.

item.description: A MacBook Pro (M5 Pro) owner reports that the trackpad suddenly lost its haptic feedback: the cursor still moves and press-to-click still registers, but there is no vibration, possibly after he cleaned dust out of the chassis gap the day before. The post offers no diagnosis or fix, so it is mainly a symptom report for anyone troubleshooting similar hardware.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: The author writes up roughly half a month of using Codex after switching from Cursor: Cursor was what first made AI-assisted coding feel striking, while Codex comes across as a full agent that pushes tasks forward on its own rather than just a coding assistant. Aimed at developers weighing which AI coding tool to adopt, or whether switching workflows is worth it.

item.title: [v2ex] [NAS] 群晖 NAS 被勒索后从 SSD 缓存恢复文件
item.description: After ransomware encrypted the files on his Synology NAS while he was travelling, a user recovered data from the two SSDs he had installed as cache. Having AI generate a CSV directory listing of the cache showed that most important files were still there, and he is now extracting hundreds of gigabytes. He still stresses off-site cold backups and the 3-2-1 rule.

item.title: [v2ex] [iPhone] 有没有人遇到过 iPhone 无线充电时候音效消失的情况？
item.description: A V2EX user reports that on their iPhone 18 Pro, the ring animation and "duang" chime that normally fire when the phone is placed on a wireless charger have stopped appearing. A reboot brings the sound back temporarily before it vanishes again, and the issue has persisted across iOS 27.2 beta, the 27.2 release and 27.3 beta; common workarounds like toggling silent mode did nothing. The poster is asking for the cause and a permanent fix.

item.description: NVIDIA's Auto Ontology is an open-source Python library (Apache-2.0) that builds a semantic, graph-based context layer from enterprise metadata: it generates ontologies, reconciles conflicting metric definitions across systems and produces AI-ready knowledge graphs. Agents get grounding for metrics and entities, query validation against certified definitions and lineage, plus provenance, with context served to any agent harness via MCP, CLI or API. item.title: [github_trending] D4Vinci/Scrapling
item.description: Scrapling is a Python web-scraping framework that aims to handle everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl, with documentation hosted on Read the Docs. The repository also carries an MCP name tag, hinting it can be plugged into MCP-based tooling, and it is currently trending on GitHub. Developers who want one library that scales from scraping a single page to crawling a whole site are the target audience.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 全新三端纯原生 SSH 客户端： SSH、SFTP 与 AI 尽在一个应用里，随楼依次赠送 100 位评论者 50 个$v2ex
item.description: SSHYard is a free, open-source SSH/SFTP client with a built-in AI assistant that can run commands directly on the remote host, so terminal sessions and file management stay in one window. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, is written in Go with fully native rendering and no WebView, which the author credits for its speed and low footprint. Source lives at GitHub's Licoy/sshyard; the V2EX thread hands out 50 $v2ex per floor for 100 floors.

item.title: [v2ex] [阅读] 2026 年九月 读人工智能，护眼 3 本
item.description: A September 2026 reading note covering three books: Melanie Mitchell's AI 3.0, a third-edition AI textbook and a Chinese title on eye care. The author argues anything published before 2023 misses large language models, yet these two AI books still map the lineage from perceptrons and backpropagation through ConvNets to AlphaGo, which helps explain where LLMs came from. The rest, he says, is data, compute and engineering work that only production environments can surface.

item.description: DiscImageStudio is a GPL-3.0 open-source tool written in C# on .NET 10 that converts an image into data matching the physical-layer constraints of CD, DVD and single-layer BD-R media, so an ordinary burner etches a visible picture onto the disc surface. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, and targets anyone who wants custom disc art from a standard drive.

item.description: Matt Pocock has published his personal agent skills, the set he uses daily for real engineering rather than vibe coding. They are deliberately small, composable, model-agnostic and meant to be forked and adapted, in contrast to process-owning approaches like GSD, BMAD and Spec-Kit that he says take control away from you. Aimed at developers who want a maintainable skill set for their coding agents.

item.title: [infoq] 同一个模型从 30 分到 95 分：拉开差距的不是模型，是Harness
item.description: At YC Paper Club's Harness Night, Seth Karten (Prime Agent), Jon Saad-Falcon (OpenJarvis) and the QM team argued the harness matters as much as the model: the same weights can score anywhere from 30% to 95% on ARC-AGI depending on the scaffolding around them. Karten splits context into model weights, active context plus a REPL, and filesystem state, and calls compression, a Python REPL and programmatic sub-agents non-negotiable. Saad-Falcon notes local LLMs trail frontier models by only 6 to 12

item.title: [infoq] Linux内核也能造了？Codex 11天写出13.9万行新内核，Rocky Linux 10跑起来了
item.description: Gregory Kurtzer, a CentOS co-founder and the driving force behind Rocky Linux, said on October 27, 2026 that in 11 days of what he calls Human-Directed Agentic Engineering he produced roughly 139,000 lines of code for Ginux, a standalone Rust-centric x86-64 kernel that boots Rocky Linux 10 and runs systemd. It is not a Linux fork, but it implements the Linux ABI, so unmodified binaries run on it. He cites Nicholas Carlini's 16-agent Claude C compiler as precedent.

item.description: A GitHub issue filed against Postman claims that simply opening the app on a Mac triggered unexpected changes to the reporter's coding agents, while the title alleges it silently auto-installs AI plugins and attempts to share all API data. Postman typically holds API keys and request collections for whole teams, so unannounced behavior like this matters to backend and QA people who keep credentials there. The account so far comes from the reporter alone.

item.title: [github_trending] thedotmack/claude-mem
item.description: claude-mem is a GitHub project that records everything an agent does during a session, compresses that history with AI, and injects the relevant parts back into later sessions so context carries over between runs. Its description says it works with Claude, which makes it relevant to developers running long, multi-session tasks who don't want to re-explain the background each time.

item.title: [github_trending] floci-io/floci
item.description: Floci is an open-source local cloud emulator pitched as an alternative to the AWS Local Emulator: you start it with a single docker compose up, with no account, no auth token and no feature gates, under the MIT license. It targets developers who want to exercise cloud-dependent code locally without touching a real cloud account or hitting paid tiers.

item.title: [juejin] 手机到底有没有偷听我们？我抓包了 72 小时，抓到了真凶
item.description: A developer captured 72 hours of phone traffic and found zero microphone wake-ups at the hardware level, which weakens the "my phone is listening" theory. The uncanny precognition instead traces to public NAT spatio-temporal hypergraphs (ST-GNN), modern private set intersection (PSI), and on-device micro-model feature vectorization. Useful for engineers who want to understand how targeting actually works and where the privacy line sits.

item.title: [hackernews] AI is forcing us to pay off 40 years of technical debt
item.description: A Hacker News discussion argues that AI in cybersecurity accelerates attackers and defenders alike, and in doing so exposes technical debt accumulated over 40 years in fragile legacy systems. The point is that once AI speeds up the pace of both offense and defense, the oldest patch-upon-patch systems are the first to break.

item.title: [hackernews] The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading
item.description: A Hacker News submission argues that the circulating claim "Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen" is misleading, because the experiments that read raw weights and the ones that actually fix Qwen use completely different techniques. It's a useful caution for anyone tracking weight-editing or model-surgery claims: placing two results side by side can imply a causal link that isn't there.

item.description: A Juejin post rounds up ten 'Skills' circulating in 2026 developer circles, meaning packaged skill sets for AI coding assistants rather than human expertise. Each Skill is a standardized workflow module meant to move an assistant from ad-hoc code generation to following a defined delivery process. It targets developers who want repeatable AI coding procedures instead of one-off prompts.

item.title: [juejin] 从codex转战workbuddy使用一周的感受

The author states upfront it is neither a paid promotion nor a takedown of Codex, which makes it useful for developers weighing a move between AI coding tools.

item.title: [github_trending] github/spec-kit
item.description: Spec Kit is an open source toolkit from GitHub that gives AI coding agents structured processes and reusable templates for writing a spec, fixing a bug, or assessing an idea. It targets teams trying to adopt Spec-Driven Development (SDD), so agent output follows a spec instead of improvisation. Docs live on GitHub Pages, and the README ships in Chinese, Japanese, and Korean as well as English.

item.title: [hackernews] Jailbreaking my car's navigation system just so I can change the time
item.description: The author drives a 2014 Renault Latitude and was told by the previous owner that changing the clock required a navigation map SD card. He didn't believe it, skipped the card, ended up with a permanent "No maps found!" message, and jailbroke the head unit just to set the time. It's a concrete case of car firmware tying unrelated features to stale map data.
